items.expectedFix: Add a mutual aggregate cap of at least 12 months' fees, with uncapped carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct; preferably also carve out data/security breaches, fraud and infringement of the other party's IP.
items.note: The clause mutually excludes consequential and similar damages and carves out indemnification, confidentiality and intellectual-property matters, but it contains no aggregate monetary liability cap. Direct damages therefore remain uncapped for both parties.

items.expectedFix: Add an express RevMed duty to defend and indemnify Sanofi and its affiliates against third-party IP infringement claims, with standard modification, combination and specification exclusions and procure, modify, replace or refund remedies.
items.note: RevMed indemnifies Sanofi for negligence, misconduct and material breach, with standard claim procedures. Any IP coverage is only indirect through narrow, knowledge-qualified representations concerning existing research and technology; there is no express indemnity for third-party claims that the licensed technology or Products infringe IP.

items.expectedFix: Delete the competing-product termination right or limit it to a specifically named product for no more than 12 months during the term, with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.
items.note: RevMed may terminate if Sanofi or its affiliates develop, manufacture or commercialize a defined Competing Product before the stated development milestone. This imposes a material competitive restriction on the customer, and the redacted duration and scope cannot be shown to satisfy the 12-month fallback.
This separate non-compete binds RevMed and its affiliates, not Sanofi, and therefore benefits the customer.

The exclusive licence, option and negotiation period run in Sanofi's favour and restrict RevMed. They do not require Sanofi to use RevMed as an exclusive supplier or refrain from third-party procurement.
No most-favoured-nation obligation requires Sanofi to match or extend third-party terms to RevMed.
No employee non-solicitation or no-hire restriction binds Sanofi.

items.expectedFix: Confirm or state that Sanofi may terminate on no more than 90 days' notice, preferably 30 days, without an early-termination fee and with any applicable pro-rata refund.
items.note: Sanofi has a unilateral convenience-termination right, including country-by-country and Product-by-Product termination, and RevMed has no corresponding convenience right. The notice periods are redacted, so compliance with the 30-day preference or 60–90-day fallback cannot be determined.
The agreement has no automatic-renewal mechanism or non-renewal notice window; its term instead ends when the specified payment obligations expire unless terminated earlier.

items.expectedFix: Specify exclusive New York County state and federal courts or, if arbitration is retained, disclose and set the seat in an accepted domestic jurisdiction, preferably New York.
items.note: Both the agreement and amendment use New York law, which is preferred. Disputes are generally subject to JAMS arbitration, however, and the arbitration seat is redacted, so it is not possible to confirm an acceptable New York forum or exclude a foreign seat.

Sanofi may assign to affiliates without consent and to a successor in an asset sale, merger, acquisition or similar transaction. RevMed's affiliate assignment requires Sanofi's reasonable consent, and Sanofi receives protections on RevMed's change of control and patent transfers.

items.expectedFix: Delete the Sanofi change-of-control cutoff and provide that the royalty right continues for Sanofi and its permitted successors and assigns.
items.note: A separate post-termination provision ends royalties payable to Sanofi upon a change of control of Sanofi. This causes Sanofi or its successor to lose a contractual payment stream solely because of the customer's change of control.

Regulatory approvals generated through RevMed's assigned trials are transferred to Sanofi, and Sanofi owns Product Marks during the commercial relationship. Although Joint Program Technology is jointly held, each party has an unrestricted exploitation right and, where needed, a perpetual, irrevocable, fully paid worldwide licence with sublicensing rights. Product Marks revert to RevMed only for terminated Products.

Sanofi receives an exclusive worldwide licence, may operate through affiliates, subcontract broadly and sublicense through multiple tiers, and may transfer the agreement to an M&A successor. On ordinary expiration, the licence becomes fully paid, royalty-free, perpetual and irrevocable. Other cited grants are reciprocal or termination-specific and do not materially narrow Sanofi's principal licence.

items.expectedFix: Specify no more than one audit per year on at least 15 days' written notice, during ordinary business hours, with the auditing party bearing costs unless underpayment exceeds 10%; prohibit direct systems access.
items.note: The financial audit right is mutual, limited to relevant books and records, conducted by an independent auditor and protected by confidentiality. The notice period, annual frequency and underpayment threshold for cost shifting are redacted, preventing confirmation that they meet fallback limits.
This separate regulatory/vendor-management audit right is held by Sanofi against RevMed, its affiliates and subcontractors and therefore benefits the customer.
No liquidated damages, penalties or breach-triggered minimum payments are payable by Sanofi.

items.expectedFix: Add a professional-and-workmanlike services warranty and a conformance warranty lasting at least 30 days for services and 90 days for software or deliverables, with repair, replacement or refund remedies; preferably include no-malicious-code assurance.
items.note: RevMed gives extensive ownership, authority, IP and legal-compliance representations, but there is no express professional-and-workmanlike performance or documentation-conformance warranty with a defined warranty period and repair, replacement or refund remedy. The disclaimer excludes all warranties not expressly stated.

items.expectedFix: Require at least USD 1 million E&O and USD 2 million cyber/privacy coverage, plus appropriate CGL, product liability and workers' compensation limits, with certificates available on request.
items.note: RevMed must maintain insurance, including product liability insurance, consistent with similarly situated companies and provide evidence on request. The clause specifies no minimum limits and does not expressly require professional/E&O or cyber/privacy coverage.

The cited limits cap post-termination regulatory, technical and patent-transition assistance; they are not minimum purchases, take-or-pay obligations or customer usage restrictions. No minimum purchase commitment binds Sanofi.

items.expectedFix: If Sanofi depends on data or services retained by RevMed, add reciprocal RevMed transition assistance for at least 90 days, delivery of Sanofi data within 30 days in a standard machine-readable format, and certified deletion after delivery. Otherwise confirm expressly that Sanofi already possesses all required data and no Vendor-held customer data remains.
items.note: The agreement contains extensive transition, regulatory-material, technical-assistance, inventory and clinical-trial transfer provisions. Those obligations predominantly run from Sanofi to RevMed when licensed rights revert, rather than from RevMed to Sanofi as contemplated by the customer-side playbook. There is no general RevMed obligation to export all Sanofi data in a standard machine-readable format and certify deletion, although the collaboration structure may make that requirement inapposite.
